newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CLOSING SHARE MARKET REPORT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CLOSING SHARE MARKET REPORT.

text.p: Dutch shares closed mixed on Thursday, dragging themselves up from the day's lows in a last hour rally as Wall Street extended Wednesday's 96 point gain with another rise at its opening.
The AEX share index closed 0.83 points easier at 588.60, up from an earlier session low of 586.48.

But dealers said investors mistrusted the trend on Wall Street and were happier to take their cue from markets closer to home such as London and Frankfurt, which showed solid declines. "It's not normal when Wall Street is up 100 points and we're down, you don't see that happening too often," said a trader.

Dealers said Thursday's last minute share rally was accompanied by a modest bond market recovery, which if it and the Wall Street gain held out, could pave the way for Dutch shares to gain ground on Friday.
"Maybe we can expect a rise tomorrow, but there's still a lot of caution about third quarter figures which have been a little disappointing recently," a trader said.

Others took a different view, predicting further churning between 585 and 590 on the AEX. "There's plenty of cash around but it's not a bullish market at the moment and it means we will continue to consolidate at these levels," said another dealer.

Akzo shares were down 1.60 guilders to 213.70, a two-day fall of 3.90 guilders, following results yesterday which came below many expectations. Dealers said they saw some pressure continuing on Akzo as analysts reviewed their ratings on the stock and considered cutting estimates of future results.
KLM slipped 20 cents to 41.50 guilders, adding to Wednesday's 2.10 guilder drop following Tuesday's announcement of falling first half operating profit and a cost cutting plan.
"Mr Bouw (the KLM chief executive) has set some ambitious and necessary targets and the market is very interested to see how he goes about achieving them," said a dealer.

Music and movies group PolyGram climbed 2.10 guilders to 79.20 on the feeling that the shares had been oversold. The shares have drifted from around 100 guilders since August, falling sharply in October after a profits warning.
Philips, 75 percent shareholder in PolyGram, was 80 cents higher at 60.80.

Unilever closed 10 cents lower at 258.60 guilders. The shares had been down to 256.40 guilders on jitters ahead of its third quarter figures due on Friday. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
